sections.heading: Area & perimeter of geometrical shapes (2D mensuration)

blocks.text: **2D mensuration** computes the **area** (space enclosed) and **perimeter** (boundary length) of plane figures — squares, rectangles, triangles, circles and their combinations.

prelimsPointers: **Square**: area a², diagonal a√2; **Rectangle**: area l×b, diagonal √(l²+b²).
Area of a rhombus = ½ × product of diagonals.

glossary.definition: The total length of the boundary of a plane figure.
A formula giving a triangle's area from its three sides via the semi-perimeter.

blocks.text: **3D mensuration** computes the **volume** (space occupied) and **surface area** of solids — cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone and sphere — frequently combined in composite-solid problems.

rows: V = ⅓πr²h; CSA = πrl (l = slant); TSA = πr(r+l).

prelimsPointers: **Cone**: V = ⅓πr²h, CSA = πrl, slant l = √(r²+h²).
Cone volume = **⅓ × cylinder** of same base & height.

glossary.definition: The sum of all outer surface areas of a solid.
The distance from a cone's apex to the edge of its base, l = √(r²+h²).

blocks.text: When a **transversal** crosses two **parallel lines**, it creates equal and supplementary angle pairs — the foundation of geometry problems on angles.

items: Angles on a straight line sum to **180°**; around a point **360°**.
Corresponding & alternate angles equal **only if lines are parallel**.

prelimsPointers: **Corresponding & alternate angles are equal** for parallel lines cut by a transversal.
Angles on a **straight line = 180°**; around a **point = 360°**.
Two lines are parallel **iff** corresponding/alternate angles are equal.

glossary.definition: A line crossing two or more other lines.
Equal angle pairs on opposite sides of a transversal between parallel lines.

blocks.text: **Triangles and quadrilaterals** have defining angle-sum and side properties used across geometry problems. A triangle's angles sum to 180°; a quadrilateral's to 360°.

rows: Angle sum = 180°; exterior angle = sum of two opposite interior; **Pythagoras** for right triangle.
Equilateral (all equal), isosceles (two equal), scalene; acute/right/obtuse.
Opposite sides equal; all angles 90°; diagonals equal & bisect.
Opposite sides & angles equal; diagonals bisect each other.
All sides equal; diagonals bisect at right angles.

prelimsPointers: **Triangle angle sum = 180°**; **exterior angle = sum of two remote interior angles**.
**Rhombus**: all sides equal, diagonals bisect at 90°.
Sum of any two sides of a triangle **> the third side**.

glossary.definition: In a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of squares of the other two sides.
A quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides parallel and equal.

blocks.text: **Algebra** uses symbols for numbers to form expressions and equations. **BODMAS** fixes the order of operations, ensuring expressions are simplified consistently.

items: Apply **BODMAS** strictly: brackets first, add/subtract last.
Memorise the **algebraic identities** for quick simplification.

prelimsPointers: Division & multiplication have **equal priority** (left to right); same for addition & subtraction.
A **linear equation** has degree 1; a **quadratic** degree 2 (two roots).

glossary.definition: The order-of-operations rule: Brackets, Orders, Division/Multiplication, Addition/Subtraction.
An equation true for all values of its variables (e.g. a²−b² = (a+b)(a−b)).

blocks.text: **'Weird symbol' problems** define a **custom operator** (e.g. a★b = a²+b) and ask you to evaluate expressions using it. The trick is to **substitute the definition exactly** and then apply normal BODMAS.

rows: Note precisely what the symbol does (e.g. a@b = 2a − b).
Replace the operator with its definition for the given values.
Replace given symbols (+ means ×, etc.) then compute.

items: Substitute the **exact definition**; don't assume conventional meaning.
For **symbol-substitution** ('if + means ÷…'), swap first, then BODMAS.

prelimsPointers: In **'if + means ×'** questions, **replace symbols first**, then apply BODMAS.
Keep track of **order** — custom operators may not be commutative.
Recheck by substituting the final values back.

glossary.definition: A specially defined symbol (e.g. a★b) whose meaning is given in the question.
A problem type where standard symbols are reassigned new meanings before evaluation.
